summary: Preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: package.json declares preinstall: "node setup.mjs", which auto-runs on npm install. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style (_0xNNN identifiers, string-map dictionaries) and downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods the binary executable, then execFileSyncs that freshly-downloaded Bun binary against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB single-line file marked "// @bun @bun-cjs" consisting of a large hex/int/string dictionary plus a string-array rotation function (the canonical obfuscator.io shape), not the auto-generated TypeScript REST client code the package advertises. The combination — obfuscated preinstall dropper + alternate-runtime fetch + execution of an obfuscated Bun-only blob at install time — is an alternate-runtime dropper: the actually-executed code path is invisible to Node-based supply-chain scanners because it runs under a downloaded runtime, and the payload itself is obfuscated to prevent inspection. This pattern in an auto-generated API client package has no legitimate build-time purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
